summary: PR #261 (CASSSIDECAR-347) caches the merged allowed+excluded metric map in FilteringMetricRegistry.getMetrics(), invalidates it on register/remove/excluded-metric add, and caches the hash code in PeriodicTaskExecutor.PeriodicTaskKey. I read the whole diff (medium tier) and applied the bundle checklists (resources.md, sidecar CONTRIBUTING.md and OPENAPI.md) plus the Sidecar '### cass-persistence-compat' lens notes. There is no REST, schema, config, serialization or file IO change, so those items do not apply. The checks that mattered were the invalidation ordering against getMetrics and the lock ordering (no deadlock found: getMetrics only iterates the ConcurrentHashMap). One real defect found: the cache is invalidated before the excluded metric is inserted, so a concurrent getMetrics can cache a map without it. Not reviewed: nothing (test file skimmed only).

findings.title: Invalidate allMetrics after the excluded metric is inserted, not inside computeIfAbsent
findings.rule: Observability: metrics registered once, registry state consistent; cache invalidation must follow the mutation
findings.problem: addExcludedMetricIfNotExists sets allMetrics = null inside the computeIfAbsent mapping function, which runs before the entry is put into excludedMetrics. A concurrent getMetrics() that runs between the null-out and the insertion sees allMetrics == null, rebuilds the map from excludedMetrics without the new entry, and caches it. Nothing invalidates it afterwards, so the excluded metric is missing from getMetrics() until some later register/remove/new excluded metric. getMetrics() is documented to include excluded metrics 'to prevent re-registering of excluded metrics', so callers (e.g. code checking getMetrics() before register) can re-register the metric or report incomplete data, with no error. The new concurrency test does not exercise this window.
findings.fix: Invalidate after the insert: call excludedMetrics.computeIfAbsent(...) with a pure mapping function, and if the returned instance is the newly created one (or simply always when the key was absent), then synchronized(this){ allMetrics = null; }. Alternatively do the put and the invalidation in one synchronized block on the same lock getMetrics() uses, or use a version counter compared when publishing the rebuilt map.
